subject: maths
title: Lines of Symmetry
seo_title: Year 4 Lines of Symmetry Worksheets: Mirror Lines in Shapes and Grids (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Identify lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes presented in different orientations; complete a simple symmetric figure with respect to a specific line of symmetry.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 lines of symmetry worksheets for the National Curriculum: test mirror lines, count lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes, spot them in turned shapes, complete symmetrical pictures on a grid, and find symmetry in flags, road signs and letters. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A mirror line splits a shape into two halves that fit exactly when folded – whichever way the shape is turned.
key_sub: A square has 4 mirror lines, a rectangle only 2, a parallelogram none. Turning a shape does not change its mirror lines; they just slant.
body_html:
What is a line of symmetry?

A line of symmetry (also called a mirror line) splits a shape into two halves that fit exactly on top of each other when you fold along it. Each half is a mirror image of the other.

To test a line, imagine folding the shape along it, or stand a small mirror on the line: if the reflection shows the whole shape, it is a mirror line.

Count every mirror line

Try every way to fold: up and down, across and slanting. A shape can have many mirror lines, one, or none.

ShapeLines of symmetry
Square4
Rectangle (not a square)2
Rhombus (not a square)2 (corner to corner)
Equilateral triangle3
Isosceles triangle1
Scalene triangle0
Kite1
Isosceles trapezium1
Parallelogram (slanting sides)0
Regular pentagon, hexagon, octagon5, 6, 8 (as many as the sides)
CircleInfinitely many

Turned shapes

Turning a shape does not change how many mirror lines it has. The lines simply turn with the shape, so they may now slant. Do not look only for lines that go straight up and down.

Complete a symmetrical picture

Give every shaded square a partner on the other side of the mirror line, the same number of squares away from the line. Count from the mirror line, not from the edge of the grid. Flip the half; do not slide it.

With a diagonal mirror line, each square’s partner is straight across the line at a right angle, the same distance away. Its row and column numbers swap over.

Worked example

How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?

3 lines join opposite corners. 3 more join the middles of opposite sides. 3 + 3 = 6.

Answer: 6

Worked example

A rectangle is turned so its sides slant. How many mirror lines does it have now?

Turning does not change the shape. It is still a rectangle, so its 2 mirror lines just slant too.

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting a rectangle’s diagonals as mirror linesFold on a diagonal: the corners stick out. A rectangle has 2
Saying a parallelogram has 2 linesIts diagonals cut it in half, but the halves do not fit. It has 0
Looking only for vertical linesMirror lines can go across or slant, especially on turned shapes
Sliding the half when completing a pictureFlip it: each square goes the same distance on the other side
Counting squares from the edge of the gridCount from the mirror line on both sides

faq.q: What do Year 4 children learn about symmetry?
faq.a: In the National Curriculum, Year 4 pupils find lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes, including shapes that are turned, and complete a simple symmetrical figure using a given mirror line.

faq.q: Is a mirror line the same as a line of symmetry?
faq.a: Yes. Both names mean a line that splits a shape into two halves that match exactly when folded. If you stand a mirror on it, the reflection completes the shape.

faq.q: Does a rectangle have 4 lines of symmetry?
faq.a: No. A rectangle that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry: up and down, and across. Its diagonals split it in half, but the halves do not fit when folded.

faq.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
faq.a: Infinitely many. Any straight line through the centre of a circle is a line of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
items.e: A square has 4 mirror lines: one up and down, one across and 2 along the diagonals, from corner to corner. Pupils often forget the diagonals.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle has 2 mirror lines: up and down, and across, through the middles of the sides. A diagonal splits it into 2 equal triangles, but they do not fit when folded, so the diagonals do not count.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (3 equal sides) have?
items.e: Each mirror line goes from a corner to the middle of the side opposite. 3 corners, so 3 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle (2 equal sides) have?
items.e: Only the line from the top corner to the middle of the bottom side works: 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a scalene triangle (no equal sides) have?
items.e: The 3 sides are all different lengths, so no fold makes the halves fit. 0 lines of symmetry.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
items.e: Any straight line through the centre of a circle is a mirror line. You could never draw them all, so a circle has infinitely many.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus have?
items.e: This rhombus (not a square) has 2 mirror lines, both from corner to corner. Lines through the middles of the sides do not work.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram have?
items.e: A parallelogram with slanting sides has 0 mirror lines. Its diagonals and its middle lines split it into equal halves, but none of them fit when folded.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
items.e: Only the line from the top corner to the bottom corner works, so a kite has 1 mirror line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles trapezium have?
items.e: Only the up-and-down line through the middles of the top and bottom works. Folding across does not, because the top is shorter than the bottom: 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
items.e: Each mirror line goes from a corner to the middle of the side opposite. 5 corners, so 5 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
items.e: 3 lines join opposite corners and 3 more join the middles of opposite sides: 3 + 3 = 6 lines.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
items.e: 4 lines join opposite corners and 4 join the middles of opposite sides: 4 + 4 = 8 lines.
Only the line straight up through the middle of the flat side works: 1 line. Folding across puts the curve on the flat side.
An oval has 2 mirror lines: one across the long way and one up and down. Slanting lines do not work, because it is not a circle.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this cross (all 4 arms the same) have?
items.e: Up and down and across both work, and so do the 2 slanting lines through the inside corners: 4 lines, just like a square.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 3 lines of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (square) 4 lines, B (equilateral triangle) 3 lines, C (rectangle) 2 lines, D (isosceles triangle) 1 line. So the answer is B.

items.q: Which shape has no lines of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (kite) 1 line, B (rhombus) 2 lines, C (rectangle) 2 lines, D (parallelogram) 0 lines. So the answer is D.

items.q: Which shape has the most lines of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (regular octagon) 8 lines, B (square) 4 lines, C (regular pentagon) 5 lines, D (regular hexagon) 6 lines. So the answer is A.

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 line of symmetry?
items.e: Count the mirror lines of each shape: A (rhombus) 2 lines, B (rectangle) 2 lines, C (kite) 1 line, D (parallelogram) 0 lines. So the answer is C.

items.e: Turning a shape does not change its mirror lines. It is still a square, so it has 4: one up and down and one across (these now join the corners), plus 2 slanting ones.

items.q: This rectangle has been turned. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: It is still a rectangle, so it still has 2 mirror lines. They have turned with it, so now they slant. Do not say 0 just because no line is straight up and down.

items.q: This isosceles triangle is lying on its side. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: The mirror line now goes across, from the corner on the right to the middle of the side on the left: 1 line.

items.q: This isosceles triangle is upside down. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Upside down, it still has the same mirror line, straight down from the middle of the top side to the bottom corner: 1 line.

items.q: This equilateral triangle has been turned a little. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: It still has 3 equal sides, so it still has 3 mirror lines, one from each corner. They are all slanting now.

items.q: This kite has been turned. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: The mirror line still joins the 2 corners where the equal sides meet. It slants now, but there is still 1 line.

items.q: This parallelogram has been turned. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: A parallelogram has 0 mirror lines, whichever way it is turned. Its diagonals split it into equal halves, but they do not fit when folded.

items.q: This right-angled triangle has 2 equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: The mirror line is slanting: from the right angle to the middle of the longest side. No line goes straight up or across, but there is still 1 line.

items.q: Both arms of this L shape are the same size. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Up and down and across do not work. The slanting line from the inside corner to the outside corner folds one arm onto the other: 1 line.

items.q: This regular hexagon has been turned. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Turning does not change the shape, so it still has 6 mirror lines: 3 join opposite corners and 3 join the middles of opposite sides.

items.q: The dashed line is a mirror line. The left half is the same in all 4 pictures. In which picture is the shape completed correctly?
items.e: Each shaded square needs a partner in the same row, the same number of squares from the mirror line on the other side. Only A is a true mirror image. Others: B: the half was turned upside down, not flipped; C: one square is missing; D: the half was slid across, not flipped (squares counted from the wrong edge).

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a column. Shade squares to the right of the line to make the picture symmetrical. How many squares will be shaded altogether?
items.e: 10 squares are shaded now. 4 of them sit on the mirror line, so each is its own partner: count them once. The other 6 each need a partner. 6 + 6 + 4 = 16.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a row. Shade squares below the line to make the picture symmetrical. How many squares will be shaded altogether?
items.e: 12 squares are shaded now. 5 of them sit on the mirror line, so each is its own partner: count them once. The other 7 each need a partner. 7 + 7 + 5 = 19.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a column. How many more squares must be shaded to make the picture symmetrical?
items.e: Squares on the mirror line are their own partners. 10 squares are shaded and 4 sit on the line, so 10 − 4 = 6 more squares.

items.q: The mirror line runs through the middle of a row. How many more squares must be shaded to make the picture symmetrical?
items.e: Squares on the mirror line are their own partners. 13 squares are shaded and 6 sit on the line, so 13 − 6 = 7 more squares.

sets.title: Symmetry in real life: flags, signs and letters

items.e: Only the line straight down the body works: each wing lands on the wing opposite. Folded across, the big top wings would land on the small bottom wings. 1 line.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this leaf have?
items.e: Fold along the middle vein: the veins on each side match. Folded across, the stalk has nothing to match, so there is just 1 line.

items.q: This flag has a cross through the middle, like the flag of England. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Fold it up and down or across: the cross lands on itself both times. The diagonals do not work, because the flag is a rectangle, not a square. 2 lines.

items.q: This flag has a cross from corner to corner, like the flag of Scotland. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: The cross runs along the diagonals, but the diagonals of a rectangle are not mirror lines. Folding up and down or across does match the 2 bands: 2 lines.

items.q: This flag has a white top half and a green bottom half. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Folding across puts white on green, so it does not work: colours must match too. Folding up and down matches white with white and green with green: 1 line.

items.q: On this flag the cross is to the left of the middle. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Folding up and down does not work, because the upright bar is not in the middle. Folding across does: 1 line.

items.q: A road sign has this shape, with no writing on it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: It is a regular octagon: 4 lines join opposite corners and 4 join the middles of opposite sides. 8 lines. (With the word STOP on it, it would have none.)

items.q: This warning sign has no picture inside yet. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: It is an equilateral triangle. Each mirror line goes from a corner to the middle of the side opposite: 3 lines.

items.q: This road sign is a red circle with a white bar across it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: A plain circle has infinitely many, but the bar spoils most of them. Only the line across and the line up and down keep the bar on itself: 2 lines.

items.q: This blue road sign has a white arrow pointing up. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
items.e: Only the line straight up through the arrow works. Folding across would put the arrow’s point on its tail: 1 line.

items.q: Which capital letter has a horizontal mirror line?
items.e: Fold E across the middle and the top arm lands on the bottom arm. M, T and V have a vertical mirror line instead.

items.q: Which capital letter has no mirror line?
items.e: F has no mirror line. H has 2, A has a vertical one and C has a horizontal one.

items.q: Which capital letter has 2 mirror lines?
items.e: X matches when folded up and down and when folded across. A and W have only a vertical line, and E only a horizontal one.
Fold Y straight down the middle and the 2 arms match. B, D and C have a horizontal line, not a vertical one.

items.q: Amelia has a square paper napkin. In how many different ways can she fold it in half so that the two halves match exactly?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: up and down, across, and the 2 diagonals. So there are 4 ways.

items.q: Harry folds a rectangular tablecloth, 2 m long and 1 m wide, from one corner to the opposite corner. Do the two halves match?
c: No, it has no mirror lines
items.e: The diagonal splits the tablecloth into 2 equal triangles, but they do not fit on top of each other, because it is not a square. A rectangle has only 2 mirror lines.

items.q: Isla says a parallelogram has 2 lines of symmetry because its diagonals cut it in half. Is she right?
items.e: Cutting a shape in half is not enough: the halves must fit when folded. Fold a slanting parallelogram any way and the corners stick out, so it has 0 lines of symmetry.

items.q: Oliver writes words in capital letters. Which word has a horizontal mirror line?
items.e: C, O, D and E each have a horizontal mirror line, so a fold across the middle of the whole word CODE works. T, Y and A only have vertical lines, and S and N have none.

items.q: Aisha cuts out a paper circle. How many different fold lines will make the two halves match?
items.e: Every line through the centre of a circle is a line of symmetry, so there are infinitely many. Up and down, across and the 2 diagonals are just 4 of them.

items.q: Poppy folds a sheet of paper in half, cuts a shape along the fold and opens it out. What must be true?
c: The fold is a mirror line
items.e: Both halves were cut at the same time, so each is the mirror image of the other. The fold is always a line of symmetry. The shape might have other mirror lines too, but it does not have to.
